Population Projections

Population projections based on 2022

On June 2025, the ONS released the Population Projections based on 2022. Several projections variants were published. The report below uses the Migration category variant.

Population Growth

From 2022 to 2032, Trafford’s population is projected to grow 4.3%, an increment of 10,161 people from 236,651 to 246,812.

England and Greater Manchester population is projected to grow more rapidly than Trafford’s, at 7.8% and 7% respectively.

Looking at broad age categories, the under 16 years Trafford’s population is projected to decrease 9.7%. England and Greater Manchester under 16 population are also projected to decrease but less than Trafford’s, at -5.8% and -6.7% respectively.

Greater Manchester’s 16-65 population is projected to grow more than England’s, however Trafford’s 16-65 population is projected to grow less than England’s.

Trafford’s population 66 or over is projected to grow but at less rate than Greater Manchester’s and both will grow less than England’s.



Trafford's population estimates

Greater Manchester authorities growth

The Greater Manchester local authorities will grow at different rates. Salford is projected to have the largest growth among them with 15.2% change and 42,468 more people from 2022 to 2032 and also is one of the local authorities with the largest growth nationally. Bury is projected to have the lowest growth with 2.1% change and 4,058 more people. Trafford will have the 4th lowest growth among GM authorities with 4.3% change and 10,162 more people.

Trafford’s population change by age

The population growth in the population pyramid reflect the growth seen in broad age categories.

For females from 2022 to 2032, the 45-49 years old group is projected to have the most increase in number with 1,498 more, whilst the 85-89 years old will have the most increase in % change with 20.3% change. The 5-9 years old group will have the most decrease in number with 1,340 less, also the 5-9 years old will have the most decrease in % change with -20.4% change.

For males, the 45-49 years old group will have the most increase in number with 1,288 more, whilst the 90+ years old will have the most increase in % change with 21.6% change. The 5-9 years old group will have the most decrease in number with 1,340 less, also the 5-9 years old will have the most decrease in % change with -19.7% change.

Although for most ages the population changes are mostly mirrored on female and male growth, for the 30-34 age group males numbers will increase 9.8% whilst women numbers will increase only 0.6%. For the 35-39 age group males numbers will increase 3.7% whilst women numbers will see a decrease of 5%.

Younger populations

In 2032, 22% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 25% in 2022, this is above average for England in 2032 (20%). Infants (aged 0 to 4) will fall from 6% to 5% between 2022 to 2032. Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 10% to 8%. Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 17 years) will stay around the same, at 8%.
